Landed at 6e92028. A non-finite bandwidth now yields NaN for every kernel shape, so the hasValidWeight check the module already relies on rejects all three alike; the enum's public construction path is unchanged.

MUTATION PROOF: removing the guard fails EXACTLY ONE test, with the message 'Rectangular(NaN) at d=0.0 produced 0.0, which passes hasValidWeight'. One failure and not more, so nothing depended on the old behaviour, and the failure names the defect rather than a symptom. The court also carries a positive control -- finite bandwidths must still produce usable weights -- without which it would pass against a weight() returning NaN unconditionally.

Gate in a clone: featuresJVM 59 passed, 0 failed, TEST_EXIT=0; scalafmtCheckAll FMT_EXIT=0 run last and separately. Gated files byte-identical to committed (c6679b31, 2d855589). LocallyObserved -- I authored and ran it.

Reservations on window.scala and WindowSuite.scala released with this close.
